meta.scope: Syria Batch 2 — Displacement/humanitarian, exchange-rate collapse, and remittances densification under extremely constrained conditions.

candidates.title: Internal displacement and return statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from OCHA / UNHCR and monitoring sources
candidates.description: Statistics on internal displacement and returns. An estimated 5.5 million IDPs remain displaced; returns have accelerated in some periods but large residual displacement persists. Continuously cited in every humanitarian and demographic assessment.

candidates.title: Exchange-rate and Syrian pound statistics
candidates.publisher: Central Bank of Syria / market monitoring
candidates.description: Official and parallel-market exchange rates for the Syrian pound. The pound has depreciated massively from pre-war levels (tens of thousands per USD in recent parallel readings); the gap between official and market rates and extreme inflation are structural features.

candidates.title: Remittance inflows framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from World Bank and monitoring sources
candidates.description: Framing of remittance inflows as a critical household and external-financing source. Estimates vary widely but place remittances in the multi-billion-dollar range; they support consumption and foreign-exchange availability under constrained formal flows.
candidates.notes: High-centrality external-financing densification under constrained formal capital.

candidates.title: Syria displacement–exchange–remittances densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from humanitarian, monetary and external sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding internal displacement/return statistics, exchange-rate/pound collapse, and remittance inflows into a coherent humanitarian–monetary–external layer under extremely constrained conditions.
